output.question: What lawsuits is Costco involved in?
output.answer: As of November 2026, Costco is a defendant in several proposed class actions and is also a plaintiff against the U.S. government. Its main defensive fight is four proposed consumer class actions filed in March 2026. They claim Costco passed IEEPA tariff costs on to shoppers and would then keep the government's refunds: Stockov (N.D. Ill.), Briggs (W.D. Wash.), Gower (King County Superior Court) and Ortiz (D.P.R.). Costco has moved to dismiss Stockov and Gower. No class has been certified, the Stockov motion had no ruling as of the last docket entry on Sept. 30, 2026, and plaintiffs in other tariff cases have asked the Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation to fold 25 retailer suits, including Stockov and Briggs, into one case (MDL No. 3202). Costco started the tariff dispute itself: in late November 2025 it sued the U.S. government in the Court of International Trade to get back the IEEPA tariffs it had paid. Other pending or recent cases include a January 22, 2026 class action in the Southern District of California claiming its Kirkland rotisserie chicken was falsely advertised as having 'no preservatives,' a pending grain-free dog food suit, and a $14 million settlement over misleading promotional email subject lines (Aaland, King County), with final approval set for Oct. 2, 2026. In early November 2026 a Washington federal judge dismissed a '100% de Agave' tequila labeling class action (Salisbury v. Costco) with prejudice.

key_facts.fact: Four proposed tariff-refund class actions against Costco were filed in March 2026: Stockov (N.D. Ill., No. 1:26-cv-02734, filed Mar. 11), Briggs (W.D. Wash., No. 2:26-cv-01064, filed Mar. 27), Gower (King County Superior Court, No. 26-2-08898-5 SEA) and Ortiz (D.P.R., No. 3:26-cv-01164-CVR).
Costco moved to dismiss Stockov on May 18, 2026, and also moved to dismiss Gower. The Stockov docket showed no ruling as of its latest entry on Sept. 30, 2026. No class has been certified.

Plaintiffs in other tariff cases asked the JPML to consolidate 25 retailer tariff suits, including Stockov and Briggs, as In re Retailer Tariff Litigation, MDL No. 3202. The source found no decision as of Nov. 2, 2026.

In Briggs, seven Costco members sued in the W.D. Washington, claiming Costco 'stands to recover the same tariff payments twice.' They seek restitution for customers who bought IEEPA-tariffed goods from Feb. 1, 2025 through Feb. 24, 2026.
Costco sued the U.S. government in the Court of International Trade to get a full refund of the IEEPA tariffs it had paid and to stop further collection.

On Jan. 22, 2026, two California plaintiffs filed a proposed class action in the S.D. California. They say Costco's Kirkland rotisserie chicken was falsely advertised as having 'no preservatives' even though it contains sodium phosphate and carrageenan. Costco then removed the claims from its signs.
Judge Kymberly Evanson (W.D. Wash.) dismissed the proposed class action Salisbury v. Costco over '100% de Agave' tequila labeling with prejudice, on international comity and act-of-state grounds.

Aaland v. Costco (King County Superior Court) is a $14M settlement over allegedly misleading marketing email subject lines. It was preliminarily approved June 23, 2026, and the final approval hearing was set for Oct. 2, 2026. Costco denies wrongdoing.

caveats: I could not open the Legal Proceedings section of Costco's FY2026 10-K (filed around Oct. 7, 2026). Costco may disclose other matters there, such as wage-and-hour and pixel-tracking privacy class actions, which third-party summaries mention.

I did not find the current status of Costco's own Court of International Trade case against the U.S. government. I also did not confirm from a primary source whether any refunds have been paid since the IEEPA tariffs were struck down.
I did not find a ruling on the Stockov or Gower motions to dismiss, or a JPML decision on MDL No. 3202, after early November 2026. The status of these may have changed.

The Aaland email settlement details come from a law-firm aggregator (Lawfold), not the settlement administrator or the court. I did not confirm whether final approval was granted at the Oct. 2, 2026 hearing.

Search results also mentioned other 2026 suits: a membership auto-renewal class action in California, an Orgain protein powder heavy-metals suit, a misleading discounts suit and a grain-free dog food heart-risk suit. I did not open primary pages for these, so they are not verified here.
Costco also faces many individual product liability and premises (slip-and-fall) suits. These are routine and not material on their own.
